categories.name: Options

options.summary: Restart Bun when source files change
options.detail: Bun watches the entry file and its imports. Each restart runs the program again with fresh global state.

options.summary: Reload code in the running Bun process
options.detail: An edit to the entry file or an imported source file reruns the modules. Values stored on globalThis survive the reload.

options.summary: Use Bun for Node.js scripts
options.detail: Package scripts and executables that invoke node through PATH, including a #!/usr/bin/env node shebang, use the Bun runtime.

options.summary: Hide the package script’s command line
options.detail: The script still runs and can write to stdout and stderr. A package script runs preNAME, NAME and postNAME hooks in order when defined. Arguments go to NAME. An option-looking argument after the target goes to the target. A standalone -- immediately before or after the target is consumed in both reviewed releases.

options.summary: Succeed if the requested entry point is missing
options.detail: Bun still looks for a file or executable when no package script matches. A command it finds can still exit with an error. For a bare name, a package script takes precedence over a source file, followed by a local executable. Use ./file.js to select the file explicitly.
